rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa’i reads with a ḍamma, making Moses report his own knowledge rather than address Pharaoh’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بالضم على إخباره عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are clear proofs that make Moses’ truthfulness visible, though Pharaoh persists in opposition.
rows.anchor: بينات تبصرك صدقي ولكنك تعاند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls Pharaoh diverted from good, stamped with evil, or doomed; the wording derives from what turned someone away.
rows.anchor: مصروفا عن الخير مطبوعا على الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two men’s expectations sharply differ: Pharaoh’s is sheer falsehood, while Moses’ approaches certainty through converging signs.
rows.anchor: فإن ظن فرعون كذب بحت وظن موسى يحوم حول اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading softens inna and uses a separating lām: Moses says he thinks Pharaoh ruined.
rows.anchor: على إن المخففة واللام هي الفارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh sought to dislodge Moses and his people, either by expelling them from Egypt or by killing and exterminating them throughout the land.
rows.anchor: أن يستخف موسى وقومه وينفيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reversed Pharaoh’s scheme: drowning became the means by which Pharaoh and his people were driven out together.
rows.anchor: فعكسنا عليه مكره فاستفززناه وقومه بالإغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After him means after Pharaoh himself, or after his drowning.
rows.anchor: من بعد فرعون أو إغراقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land Israel is told to inhabit is the land from which Pharaoh had tried to expel them.
rows.anchor: التي أراد أن يستفزكم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final promise may mean the return, resurrection life, the Hour, or the abode of the afterlife, specifically the resurrection.
rows.anchor: الكرة أو الحياة أو الساعة أو الدار الآخرة يعني قيام القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All will be brought together in mixed groups from varied tribes, then judged and divided into the fortunate and wretched.
rows.anchor: ثم نحكم بينكم ونميز سعداءكم من أشقيائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an was sent down in truth, for a purpose required by truth, and came to the Messenger containing truth.
rows.anchor: وما أنزلنا القرآن إلا ملتبسا بالحق المقتضي لإنزاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that angels guarded it from satanic interference during its descent and delivery to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وما أنزلناه من السماء إلا محفوظا بالرصد من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This denies that falsehood can affect the Qur’an at either end; the Messenger’s role is to promise reward to the obedient and warn sinners of punishment.
rows.anchor: نفي اعتراء البطلان له أول الأمر وآخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the Qur’an was revealed in separate installments; another takes the phrase as distinguishing truth from falsehood by eliding a preposition, as in the cited expression.
rows.anchor: نزلناه مفرقا منجما. وقيل فرقنا فيه الحق من الباطل فحذف الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with a doubled consonant emphasizes its many installments, since revelation unfolded over twenty years.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالتشديد لكثرة نجومه فإنه نزل في تضاعيف عشرين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paced recitation gives people time, making memorization easier and understanding more attainable.
rows.anchor: على مهل وتؤدة فإنه أيسر للحفظ وأعون في الفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with fatḥa in makth is a dialectal variant.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالفتح وهو لغة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its gradual sending followed the sequence of events.
rows.anchor: { ونزلنه تنزيلا } على حسب الحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether opponents believe does not add to the Qur’an’s perfection, and their refusal does not diminish it.
rows.anchor: فإن إيمانكم بالقرآن لا يزيده كمالا وامتناعكم عنه لا يورثه نقصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those already given knowledge are learned readers of earlier scriptures who recognize revelation and prophetic signs, or had found the Prophet’s description and revelation in those books.
rows.anchor: هم العلماء الذين قرؤوا الكتب السابقة وعرفوا حقيقة الوحي وأمارات النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge clause can explain the challenge or console the Prophet: take comfort in learned believers rather than fret over ignorant people’s belief or rejection.
rows.anchor: على سبيل التسلية كأنه قيل: تسل بإيمان العلماء عن إيمان الجهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prostration expresses reverence for God or gratitude that earlier scriptures’ promise of Muhammad’s mission and the Qur’an’s revelation was fulfilled.
rows.anchor: أو شكرا لإنجاز وعده في تلك الكتب ببعثه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They declare God exalted above failing to keep His promise, which was certain to come to pass.
rows.anchor: إنه كان وعده كائنا لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second prostration differs from the first: the first thanked God for fulfilled promise; this one responds to Qur’anic admonitions with tears of fear.
rows.anchor: فإن الأول للشكر عند إنجاز الوعد والثاني لما أثر فيهم من مواعظ القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chin is named because it is the first part of a face to touch the ground, and the lām specifies the place of falling.
rows.anchor: وذكر الذقن لأنه أول ما يلقى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing the Qur’an increases their reverent awe as well as their knowledge and certainty in God.
rows.anchor: كما يزيدهم علما ويقينا بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion may be that polytheists heard the Prophet say Allah and Rahman, then accused him of invoking another god; alternatively Jews said he rarely mentioned Rahman despite its prominence in the Torah.
rows.anchor: نزلت حين سمع المشركون رسول الله يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation makes the names equal in goodness of invocation and success in attaining the aim; Bayḍāwī prefers it in light of the following clause. The other equates their reference to one divine essence despite differing aspects of designation.
rows.anchor: وعلى الثاني أنهما سيان في حسن الإطلاق والإفضاء إلى المقصود وهو أجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here calling means naming: the first object is omitted, aw offers a choice, ayya’s tanwīn replaces its genitive complement, and ma reinforces its indefiniteness.
rows.anchor: والدعاء في الآية بمعنى التسمية وهو يتعدى إلى مفعولين حذف أولهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the named entity, not the name; the wording replaces an underlying statement that either call is good, emphasizing His beautiful names and their majestic and gracious attributes.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { فله } للمسمى لأن التسمية له لا للاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not recite loudly enough for polytheists to hear and revile the prayer, or so softly that fellow believers cannot hear; choose a middle course, since moderation is loved.
rows.anchor: بقراءة صلاتك حتى تسمع المشركين، فإن ذلك يحملهم على السب واللغو فيها

rows.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr whispered to privately address God who knew his need; Umar spoke aloud to repel Satan and wake sleepers, so the Prophet told Abu Bakr to raise his voice and Umar to lower his.
rows.anchor: روي أن أبا بكر رضي الله عنه كان يخفت ويقول: أناجي ربي وقد علم حاجتي، وعمر رضي الله عنه كان يجهر ويقول أطرد الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation prohibits making every prayer entirely loud or quiet, prescribing quiet recitation by day and loud recitation by night.
rows.anchor: لا تجهر بصلاتك كلها ولا تخافت بها بأسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no child, co-sharer in sovereignty and divinity, or ally sought to remove humiliation; He needs no partner or helper, by choice or necessity.
rows.anchor: ولي يواليه من أجل مذلة به ليدفعها بموالاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise belongs to God as perfect in Himself, sole creator, and absolute benefactor; all else is deficient, owned, and receives His favor.
rows.anchor: لأنه الكامل الذات المنفرد بالإيجاد، المنعم على الإطلاق وما عداه ناقص مملوك نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to magnify God reminds even the most diligent worshipper that human praise and glorification fall short of His due.
rows.anchor: ينبغي أن يعترف بالقصور عن حقه في ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly taught this verse to boys of Banu Abd al-Muttalib once they could speak clearly.
rows.anchor: روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا أفصح الغلام من بني عبد المطلب علمه هذه الآية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet promises a qinṭār in Paradise to one whose heart softens at mention of parents when reciting Bani Isra’il; Bayḍāwī defines it as 1,200 uqiyyas.
rows.anchor:
وعنه عليه السلام
" من قرأ سورة بني إسرائيل فرق قلبه عند ذكر الوالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is the greatest divine favor because it guides people to perfection and to what orders worldly and afterlife welfare.
rows.anchor: رتب استحقاق الحمد على إنزاله تنبيها على أنه أعظم نعمائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It has no flaw in wording, contradiction in meaning, or deviation from truth; semantic crookedness parallels crookedness in physical things.
rows.anchor: اختلال في اللفظ وتناف في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qayyiman means balanced and straight, with neither excess nor deficiency; alternatively it manages human welfare, completes its description after perfection, or confirms earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: مستقيما معتدلا لا إفراط فيه ولا تفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically qayyiman depends on an understood verb meaning He made it so, or is circumstantial from lahu or al-kitab; if wa is circumstantial rather than conjunctive, the wording entails fronting and delay.
rows.anchor: وانتصابه بمضمر تقديره جعله قيما أو على الحال من الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning omits its first object, those who disbelieve, because context supplies it and the passage focuses on the warning itself.
rows.anchor: فحذف المفعول الأول اكتفاء بدلالة القرينة واقتصارا على الغرض المسوق إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min ladunhu means issued from God’s presence.
rows.anchor: { من لدنه } صادرا من عنده

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr reads the dāl quiescent with ishām to indicate its original vowel, then breaks the nūn for meeting of two quiescent letters and the hāʾ by assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر بإسكان الدال كإسكان الباء من سبع مع الإشمام ليدل على أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ good reward is Paradise.
rows.anchor: { ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصلحات أن لهم أجرا حسنا } هو الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers remain in the promised reward forever, without interruption.
rows.anchor: في الأجر. { أبدا } بلا انقطاع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who say God took a child are singled out and warned again because their disbelief is especially grave; the warning’s object is omitted because it was already stated.
rows.anchor: { وينذر الذين قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا } خصهم بالذكر وكرر الإنذار متعلقا بهم استعظاما لكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claimed knowledge may concern the child, adoption, or the assertion: they speak from ignorance, false conjecture, or inherited usage in which father and child mean cause and effect; alternatively, they do not know God, or would not attribute adoption to Him.
rows.anchor: أي بالولد أو باتخاذه أو بالقول، والمعنى أنهم يقولونه عن جهل مفرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fathers likewise lacked knowledge of the adoption claim.
rows.anchor: { ولا لآبائهم } الذين تقولوه بمعنى التبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statement is enormously blasphemous because it likens and associates God and implies He needs a child to help or succeed Him.
rows.anchor: عظمت مقالتهم هذه في الكفر لما فيها من التشبيه والتشريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalimatan is accusative as specification; a nominative subject reading is reported, but the accusative better conveys the intended point.
rows.anchor: نصب على التمييز وقرىء بالرفع على الفاعلية والأول أبلغ وأدل على المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about words issuing from their mouths intensifies the audacity of uttering them; air literally carries the words. Alternatively it describes an omitted subject because the verb is a blame formula, and a reading quiesces the bāʾ with ishām.
rows.anchor: والخارج بالذات هو الهواء الحامل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bākhiʿ nafsaka means killing oneself; the Prophet grieves at their turning away as someone bereaved grieves after loved ones depart.
rows.anchor: لما يداخله من الوجد على توليهم بمن فارقته أعزته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading annexes nafs to bākhiʿ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { بخع نفسك } على الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-asaf means extreme grief and anger, either grief for them or being in a state of grief for them.
rows.anchor: والأسف فرط الحزن والغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥadīth here means the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: { إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث } بهذا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening an is read with fatḥa to mean because; bākhiʿ cannot govern it unless the statement narrates a past state.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «أن» بالفتح على لأن فلا يجوز إعمال «باخع»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What adorns the earth includes animals, plants, and minerals; it is an adornment for the earth and its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: { إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض } من الحيوان والنبات والمعادن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test asks who uses worldly adornment best: one not deceived, content with what suffices, and spending it properly; this also consoles the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهو من زهد فيه ولم يغتر به وقنع منه بما يزجي به أيامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse discourages attachment to worldly adornment by promising to turn it into earth and leave the surface smooth and barren.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إنا لنعيد ما عليها من الزينة ترابا مستويا بالأرض ونجعله كصعيد أملس لا نبات فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jarz is land whose vegetation has been cut away, from the verb meaning to cut.
rows.anchor: والجرز الأرض التي قطع نباتها. مأخوذ من الجرز وهو القطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am here means bal, ‘rather’: the question asks whether the People of the Cave and Raqim were extraordinarily preserved alive for a long time.
rows.anchor: { أم حسبت } بل أحسبت. { أن أصحب الكهف والرقيم } في إبقاء حياتهم مدة مديدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their story is no great wonder compared with God’s creation of countless species from one substance with diverse natures and forms, then returning them to it.
rows.anchor: على طبائع متباعدة وهيئات متخالفة تعجب الناظرين من مادة واحدة، ثم ردها إليها ليس بعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kahf is a spacious cave in a mountain.
rows.anchor: { الكهف } الغار الواسع في الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raqim may name the mountain or valley containing their cave, their town, their dog, or the lead or stone tablet on which their names were inscribed at its entrance.
rows.anchor: { الرقيم } اسم الجبل أو الوادي الذي فيه كهفهم

rows.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
rows.claim: Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt’s verse is cited as poetic evidence for Raqim as a name associated with the cave people.
rows.anchor:
قال أمية بن أبي الصلت:
وليس بها إلا الرقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the Raqim people were three travelers provisioning their families; rain drove them into a cave and a boulder blocked its entrance.
rows.anchor: وقيل أصحاب الرقيم قوم آخرون كانوا ثلاثة خرجوا يرتادون لأهلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the account later attributed to Nuʿman ibn Bashir, one man paid a worker fully, invested abandoned wages in livestock, returned the multiplied herd, and prayed; the boulder shifted.
rows.anchor: استعملت أجراء ذات يوم فجاء رجل وسط النهار وعمل في بقيته مثل عملهم فأعطيته مثل أجرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the same account, a man refused a woman who offered herself after she invoked fear of God, gave her requested help, and prayed; the cave opened further.
rows.anchor: أصابت الناس شدة، فجاءتني امرأة فطلبت مني معروفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third man waited with milk rather than wake his aged parents; he served them at dawn, prayed, and God opened the cave for them all to leave.
rows.anchor: فوجدتهما نائمين فشق علي أن أوقظهما، فتوقعت جالسا ومحلبي على يدي حتى أيقظهما الصبح فسقيتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī says the account was transmitted by Nuʿman ibn Bashir.
rows.anchor: ففرج الله عنهم فخرجوا وقد رفع ذلك نعمان بن بشير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the townspeople discover or overpower the youths, the pronoun refers to the people implied in their address; they could kill them by stoning.
rows.anchor: أي يطلعوا عليكم أو يظفروا بكم، والضمير للأهل المقدر في { أيها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning them to the townspeople’s religion means forcing them into it; alternatively, they had first followed that religion before believing.
rows.anchor: أو يصيروكم إليها كرها من العود بمعنى الصيرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they re-enter that religion, they will never prosper.
rows.anchor: { ولن تفلحوا إذا أبدا } إن دخلتم في ملتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicted speakers are people discussing the youths’ story in the Prophet’s time, among the People of the Book and believers.
rows.anchor: أي الخائضون في قصتهم في عهد الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: The three-and-dog claim is attributed either to Jews or to the Jacobite leader among Christians of Najran.
rows.anchor: قيل هو قول اليهود وقيل هو قول السيد من نصارى نجران

rows.speaker: النصارى
rows.claim: The five-and-dog claim is attributed either to Christians or their Nestorian al-ʿAqib.
rows.anchor: قاله النصارى أو العاقب منهم وكان نسطوريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb means offering an unseen report without access to it, or conjecturing, as in the expression for guessing by supposition.
rows.anchor: يرمون رميا بالخبر الخفي الذي لا مطلع لهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first two reports omit the future marker because it need not be repeated after conjunction with the construction already containing it.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يذكر بالسين اكتفاء بعطفه على ما هو فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven-and-dog view is correct: Muslims learned it from the Prophet via Gabriel, and the wording signals it; the earlier two views are called guesses, while the conjunction marks the dog’s firmly attached description.
rows.anchor: إنما قاله المسلمون بإخبار الرسول لهم عن جبريل عليهما الصلاة والسلام وإيماء الله تعالى إليه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports seven youths—Yamlikha, Makshaliniya, Mashliniya, Marnush, Dabarnush, Shadhnush, and a shepherd—with their dog Qitmir in Ephesus.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه هم سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم وأسماؤهم: يمليخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view attributes all three competing counts to the People of the Book, with only a few knowing the matter.
rows.anchor: وقيل الأقوال الثلاثة لأهل الكتاب والقليل منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Debate only openly from the Qur’anic account without insulting or deeply disputing; do not seek their guidance because revelation suffices and they lack knowledge, or question them merely to expose them against good manners.
rows.anchor: فلا تجادل في شأن الفتية إلا جدالا ظاهرا غير متعمق فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second inna clause predicates the first; its referent may be omitted, unnecessary because the universal ‘who does good’ covers it, or replaced by the explicit expression because only believers doing good truly fit it.
rows.anchor: خبر إن الأولى وهي الثانية بما في حيزها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paradise description between the clauses is parenthetical; grammatically it either explains the reward or serves as a second predicate.
rows.anchor: وما بينهما اعتراض وعلى الأول استئناف لبيان الأجر أو خبر ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the bracelets, the first min marks origin and the second explains the noun; their indefinite form magnifies beauty, and asawir is a plural of aswira or aswar from siwar.
rows.anchor: وتنكيره لتعظيم حسنها من الإحاطة به وهو جمع أسورة أو أسوار في جمع سوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wear green because it is the most beautiful and freshest color.
rows.anchor: لأن الخضرة أحسن الألوان وأكثرها طراوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is fine silk and istabraq thick silk; their combination signifies that Paradise offers everything souls desire and eyes find pleasing.
rows.anchor: مما رق من الديباج وما غلظ منه جمع بين النوعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reclining on couches is the posture of people enjoying luxury; the reward is Paradise and its bliss, and its couches are an excellent place to rest.
rows.anchor: على السرر كما هو هيئة المتنعمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable is for disbeliever and believer; one account identifies Israelite brothers Qatrus and Judah, who split an inheritance of 8,000 dinars: one bought estates while the other spent on good works.
rows.anchor: هما أخوان من بني إسرائيل كافر اسمه قطروس ومؤمن اسمه يهوذا، ورثا من أبيهما ثمانية آلاف دينار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another identification makes them brothers from Banu Makhzum: unbeliever al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad and believer Abu Salama Abd Allah, later husband of Umm Salama before the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل الممثل بهما أخوان من بني مخزوم كافر وهو الأسود بن عبد الأشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens are two grape orchards, and the complete phrase explains the parable or describes the men.
rows.anchor: من كروم والجملة بتمامها بيان للتمثيل أو صفة للرجلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Date palms surrounded the grape gardens; grammatically the bā gives the verb a second object.
rows.anchor: وجعلنا النخل محيطة بهما مؤزرا بها كرومهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crops between the gardens made each orchard supply both staples and fruits, with continuous cultivation arranged beautifully.
rows.anchor: ليكون كل منهما جامعا للأقوات والفواكه متواصل العمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each garden yielded its full produce without the decrease common to orchards whose fruit varies from year to year.
rows.anchor: { ولم تظلم منه } ولم تنقص من أكلها. { شيئا } يعهد في سائر البساتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading says kull al-jannatayn instead of kilta al-jannatayn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «كل الجنتين آتى أكله»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The river ensures lasting irrigation, their essential need, and increases the gardens’ beauty.
rows.anchor: ليدوم شربهما فإنه الأصل ويزيد بهاؤهما

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqub reads the river-flow verb in a lighter form.
rows.anchor: شربهما فإنه الأصل ويزيد بهاؤهما، وعن يعقوب «وفجرنا» بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamar means other kinds of property besides the gardens; ʿĀṣim opens both consonants, Abu ʿAmr dammas the first and quiesces the second, and others damma both, also at 18:42.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم بفتح الثاء والميم، وأبو عمرو بضم الثاء وإسكان الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥāwaratan means returning speech in dialogue, from the root meaning to return.
rows.anchor: يراجعه في الكلام من حار إذا رجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafar means retinue and supporters, or male children because they accompany him.
rows.anchor: حشما وأعوانا. وقيل أولادا ذكورا لأنهم الذين ينفرون معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He enters with his companion to tour and boast; the singular garden can represent all his worldly possessions since he has no share in Paradise, because the gardens are contiguous, or because he enters them one by one.
rows.anchor: وإفراد الجنة لأن المراد ما هو جنته وما متع به من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wrongs himself through conceit and disbelief, and thinks his garden will never perish because of long hopes and heedless delusion.
rows.anchor: ضار لها بعجبه وكفره { قال ما أظن أن تبيد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He denies the Hour and supposes that, if returned to his Lord as the believer claims, he will find a better destination than his garden.
rows.anchor: بالبعث كما زعمت. { لأجدن خيرا منها } من جنته

rows.speaker: الحجازيان والشامي
rows.claim: The Hijazi and Shami readers say ‘better than the two gardens’ rather than ‘better than it.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحجازيان والشامي «منهما» أي من الجنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He swears this because he thinks God granted his wealth as something he deserves in himself, and assumes he will have it wherever he goes.
rows.anchor: لاعتقاده أنه تعالى إنما أولاه لاستئهاله واستحقاقه إياه لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dust is the source material of the man himself or his first ancestor; sperm is his immediate material, and God then completed him as an adult male.
rows.anchor: ثم عدلك وكملك إنسانا ذكرا بالغا مبلغ الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying resurrection amounts to disbelief in God because it doubts His power; creating man from dust establishes His ability to recreate him from it.
rows.anchor: جعل كفره بالبعث كفرا بالله تعالى لأن منشأه الشك في كمال قدرة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakinna originates as lakin ana; dropping the hamza, with or without transferring its vowel, brings two nūns together and causes assimilation.
rows.anchor: أصله لكن أنا فحذفت الهمزة بنقل الحركة أو دونه فتلاقت النونان فكان الإدغام

rows.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqūb in one transmission retain the alif in connected speech, to replace the hamza or by treating connection like pause; a reading also preserves the original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب في رواية بالألف في الوصل لتعويضها من الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may be a pronoun of the matter, with its clause as predicate and that construction predicating ana; alternatively it refers to God, with Allah as apposition and rabbi as predicate.
rows.anchor: وهو ضمير الشأن وهو بالجملة الواقعة خبرا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause counters the companion’s disbelief: you disbelieve, but I believe in God; variants include lakin huwa Allah rabbi and wa-lakin ana la ilaha illa huwa rabbi.
rows.anchor: والاستدراك من أكفرت كأنه قال: أنت كافر بالله لكني مؤمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer hopes God will grant him something better than the garden, in this world or the next, because of his faith; this answers the condition.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا أو في الآخرة لإيماني وهو جواب الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The storm is sent against the garden because of its owner’s disbelief; ḥusbān may be projectiles such as lightning bolts, or a reckoning meaning divinely measured destruction or punishment for bad deeds.
rows.anchor: مرامي جمع حسبانة وهي الصواعق. وقيل هو مصدر بمعنى الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It becomes a slick, level surface after its plants and trees are destroyed.
rows.anchor: أرضا ملساء يزلق عليها باستئصال نباتها وأشجارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghawran means sunk deep in the earth; the verbal noun is used adjectivally, like zalq.
rows.anchor: أي غائرا. في الأرض مصدر وصف به كالزلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will be unable to search for the vanished water and restore it.
rows.anchor: للماء الغائر ترددا في رده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read yakun in the masculine, referring back to the preceding subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالياء لتقدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No group could help him by preventing destruction, restoring what was destroyed, or producing its like; only God has that power.
rows.anchor: يقدرون على نصره بدفع الإهلاك أو رد المهلك أو الإتيان بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He could not protect himself by his own strength from God’s retribution.
rows.anchor: وما كان ممتنعا بقوته عن انتقام الله منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There means that place and circumstance; God’s support alone can avail, or He supports believing allies against unbelievers as in the two-garden story.
rows.anchor: النصرة له وحدة لا يقدر عليها غيره تقديرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best reward and best final outcome for His allies.
rows.anchor: { هو خير ثوابا وخير عقبا } أي لأوليائه

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: With the initial wāw kasra, wilāya means dominion or sovereignty: God’s rule cannot be overcome or resisted; alternatively it signals that none but Him should be worshipped.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالكسر ومعناه السلطان والملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worship interpretation recalls the verse about sailors calling God alone in distress, suggesting the ruined man’s wish not to have associated was uttered under compulsion and panic.
rows.anchor: كان عن اضطرار وجزع مما دهاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There may also point to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل { هنالك } إشارة إلى الآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: They read al-ḥaqq in the nominative as an adjective of wilāya; an accusative reading makes it an emphatic verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو والكسائي { الحق } بالرفع صفة للولاية، وقرىء بالنصب على المصدر المؤكد

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza quiesce the bāʾ in ʿuqban; ʿuqbā is also read, and all forms mean the final outcome.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة «عقبا» بالسكون، وقرىء «عقبى» وكلها بمعنى العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may uproot and move the mountains through the air or remove them until they become scattered dust; the day phrase may attach to ‘with your Lord’ in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: واذكر يوم نقلعها ونسيرها في الجو، أو نذهب بها فنجعلها هباء منبثا

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read tusayyar in the feminine passive; another reading has it from the verb ‘to move.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر تسير بالتاء والبناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is exposed after the mountains are removed, with nothing left to cover it; a passive reading of tara is also reported.
rows.anchor: بادية برزت من تحت الجبال ليس عليها ما يسترها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense ‘We gathered’ confirms certainty, or indicates that people are gathered before the mountains move so they can witness the promised scene; then the wāw is circumstantial with an implied qad.
rows.anchor: لتحقق الحشر أو للدلالة على أن حشرهم قبل التسيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nughādir means leave behind; related words refer to abandoning a pledge and water left by a flood, and a reading uses the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: { فلم نغادر } فلم نترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their presentation before God resembles troops arrayed before a ruler, not so He can identify them but so He can decide their fate.
rows.anchor: شبه حالهم بحال الجند المعروضين على السلطان لا ليعرفهم بل ليأمر فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They stand in a row so that none conceals another.
rows.anchor: مصطفين لا يحجب أحد أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You have come to Us’ can have an implicit speech verb, functioning circumstantially or governed by the mention of the Day.
rows.anchor: على إضمار القول على وجه يكون حالا أو عاملا في يوم نسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They come as first created either naked without property or children, as in ‘you came singly,’ or alive as in their first creation.
rows.anchor: { كما خلقنكم أول مرة } عراة لا شيء معكم من المال والولد كقوله { ولقد جئتمونا فرادى } أو أحياء كخلقتكم الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had claimed no appointed time would be made for resurrection and that the prophets had lied; bal marks a transition to a new topic.
rows.anchor: وقتا لإنجاز الوعد بالبعث والنشور وأن الأنبياء كذبوكم به، وبل للخروج من قصة إلى أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book may be records placed in right and left hands, records in the balance, or a metaphor for the reckoning.
rows.anchor: صحائف الأعمال في الأيمان والشمائل أو في الميزان وقيل هو كناية عن وضع الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals fear the sins recorded in it, and ‘O our ruin’ addresses their destruction; their question expresses astonishment.
rows.anchor: ينادون هلكتهم التي هلكوها من بين الهلكات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither a minor nor a major deed is omitted: every deed is counted and encompassed.
rows.anchor: { لا يغادر صغيرة } هنة صغيرة. { ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها } إلا عددها وأحاط بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They find their deeds present in writing in the records.
rows.anchor: { ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا } مكتوبا في الصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not wrong anyone by recording an act they did not do or increasing punishment beyond what their deed merits.
rows.anchor: فيكتب عليه ما لم يفعل أو يزيد في عقابه الملائم لعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam prostration story recurs as a preface; here it censures boastful people by showing that their conduct follows Iblis, or counters worldly allure by pointing to its passing and Satan’s ancient enmity.
rows.anchor: ها هنا لما شنع على المفتخرين واستقبح صنيعهم قرر ذلك بأنه من سنن إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis being from the jinn is circumstantial or explains his refusal; it proves angels never disobey and Iblis was originally a jinni.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن الملك لا يعصى ألبتة وإنما عصى إبليس لأنه كان جنيا في أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasaqa ʿan amri rabbih means he departed from God’s command by refusing to prostrate; the fa marks causation.
rows.anchor: فخرج عن أمره بترك السجود والفاء للسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about taking Iblis and his progeny as allies is an incredulous rebuke; his progeny may mean children or followers, figuratively called descendants.
rows.anchor: والهمزة للإنكار والتعجب. { وذريته } أولاده أو أتباعه، وسماهم ذرية مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking them as allies means replacing obedience to God with obedience to them; Iblis and his progeny are a wretched substitute for God.
rows.anchor: فتستبدلونهم بي فتطيعونهم بدل طاعتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not make Iblis and his offspring witnesses to creation of the heavens, earth, or one another, showing He did not rely on them; calling them misleaders condemns them.
rows.anchor: ليدل على نفي الاعتضاد بهم في ذلك كما صرح به بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to polytheists: they witnessed neither creation nor inaccessible knowledge, so their claim that people would follow them if they believed is baseless; do not seek their aid for religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير للمشركين والمعنى: ما أشهدتهم خلق ذلك وما خصصتهم بعلوم لا يعرفها غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The latter view is supported by a reading addressing the Prophet directly; another reading retains the original form of muttakhidh.
rows.anchor: ويعضده قراءة من قرأ { وما كنت } على خطاب الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAḍudan has readings with a lighter form and following vowel, and a plural form meaning supporters, from the verb ‘to strengthen.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء { متخذا المضلين } على الأصل و { عضدا } بالتخفيف و { عضدا } بالاتباع و { عضدا } كخدم جمع عاضد
